decisive_join: Recover the binding high-risk classification and provider/deployer architecture while preserving the amended 2027 application date and refusing to report delayed duties as operative on 2026-08-01.

findings.claim: The EU AI Act retains employment recruitment and worker-management systems as high-risk categories.
limits: Classification of a named system depends on its intended purpose, operator role, exclusions, and actual deployment.

findings.claim: The recovered operator architecture assigns distinct provider and deployer burdens, including qualified human oversight and authority to disregard or reverse outputs.
limits: The duties are recorded as scheduled, not operative, for the delayed Annex III employment regime on the wave date.

findings.claim: Notice and meaningful explanation are part of the future covered decision transaction; they are not equivalent to model-source-code disclosure or automatic reversal.
limits: The exact decision, system classification, person, and explanation content remain unrecovered.

findings.claim: Reporting the delayed high-risk employment duties as presently operative on 2026-08-01 would be false; the current application date is 2027-12-02.
limits: Other AI Act provisions have different dates and are not exhaustively adjudicated in this lane.

observations.notes: AI systems used for recruitment, candidate selection, employment decisions, task allocation, monitoring, or evaluation are designated high-risk categories in Annex III.
observations.subject: EU employment AI

observations.notes: The binding architecture assigns providers technical documentation, instructions, quality-management, and post-market responsibilities for covered high-risk systems.
observations.subject: High-risk AI provider

observations.notes: Deployers must assign competent, trained, and authorized human oversight capable of understanding, disregarding, overriding, or reversing outputs where the duties apply.
observations.subject: High-risk AI deployer

observations.notes: The architecture includes workplace and affected-person notice and a right to a clear and meaningful explanation for certain decisions based on high-risk outputs.
observations.subject: Affected worker or applicant

observations.notes: Current Commission implementation material reports that Annex III high-risk obligations, including employment systems, apply from 2 December 2027 after the 2026 AI Omnibus.
observations.subject: High-risk employment obligations

observations.notes: The impact-assessment duty is role- and deployer-specific and does not automatically attach to every private employer deployment.
observations.subject: Named private employer deployment

selection_rule: Read the original Regulation together with the current Commission implementation timeline and FAQ; separate classification, future application, operator role, human oversight, notice, explanation, and impact-assessment scope.

prohibited_inferences: the delayed employment duties are operative on 2026-08-01
every private employer must perform a fundamental-rights impact assessment
an explanation requires disclosure of all protected intellectual property
high-risk classification proves illegality or harm

title: European Union high-risk employment AI operator and explanation custody
